title: 构建视觉智能——Black Forest Labs 的 Andreas Blattmann 与 Dustin Podell — Latent Space
author: swyx .ai

Not many people know that Stable Diffusion is why I went fulltime into AI (I aptly titled Multiverse, not Metaverse to call out Zuck’s mistaken investment). It turns out that Dustin Podell also had the same aha moment - quitting his day job when the model came out. But we took very different paths… I stuck to what I knew in human content creation, and Dustin immersed deep into AI content creation with Andreas Blattmann, co-inventor of Latent Diffusion and the rest of the world-leading imagegen crew at Stability AI. Stability fell apart, but Anj Midha helped the core group spin out to BFL, which immediately built an incredible new imagegen model in the Flux series. But why are they now going into video and world models?

Andreas gives an example you can try with one hand. If somebody tosses you a ball, your hand starts moving before the ball reaches you. You can do that without being able to write down the trajectory. When he talks about building visual intelligence, that’s the kind of knowledge he means. A still can show you where the ball is. A video shows you how it got there. The sound of impact can tell you when it hit something, even if the camera missed the contact. That’s BFL’s argument for training FLUX 3 on the three signals together. BFL’s FLUX 3 release

The horse in motion is one of the FLUX 3 examples we show in the intro. The audio examples are worth playing with the sound on. FLUX 3 Video

What a moving camera teaches you

Suppose the camera starts in front of a person and pans around them. At some point the model owes you the back of their head. Andreas thinks ordinary two-dimensional video contains a great deal of evidence about what objects look like from other angles. That doesn’t settle whether a model “understands physics,” a point we go back and forth on. It does give you a much better test than asking whether one frame looks convincing.

There’s a good engineering example late in the episode. Sharpen each frame of a clip independently and each frame might look terrific. Hit play and the extra detail can shimmer, because the upscaler made a slightly different decision every time. BFL derives its video upscaler from the same FLUX 3 backbone. Temporal consistency matters even when all the user asked for was a higher-resolution file.

What’s worth spending training compute on?

One of the questions I had for them was whether autoregression was taking over image generation. Andreas gives the other side its due. An autoregressive model can learn from all the tokens in a training example at once. On the diffusion side, the team can distill a long sampling process down to a handful of steps. Which advantage matters depends on whether you’re paying to train the model or waiting for an image to finish.

Dustin’s early Kontext experiment is a nice example of how they decide where to invest. He suspected an image model that could draw a dog wearing a hat already knew something about where hats go. He and a colleague collected a small set of photos labeled with relationships. A training run of a few hours got the model to put a logo on a shirt. It was rough, but it was enough to take to the next offsite. The team then spent months on the data and the model. FLUX Kontext examples

My favorite user story comes near the end. People were feeding FLUX old, degraded family photos, restoring them, then showing the pictures to their families. Dustin says he hadn’t predicted that use. After talking about preserving somebody’s identity across edits and across frames, it’s a lovely example of who actually notices if you get it right.

aiSummary: Black Forest Labs 联合创始人 Andreas Blattmann 和 Dustin Podell 探讨了 FLUX 3 的多模态训练方法、从 Stable Diffusion 到视频生成的演进，以及通过时间与音频信号构建视觉智能的愿景。
oneSentenceSummary: Black Forest Labs 联合创始人 Andreas Blattmann 和 Dustin Podell 探讨了 FLUX 3 的多模态训练方法、从 Stable Diffusion 到视频生成的演进，以及通过时间与音频信号构建视觉智能的愿景。
summary: 本文采访了 Black Forest Labs 的联合创始人 Andreas Blattmann 和 Dustin Podell，探讨他们的 FLUX 3 模型以及实验室从 Stability AI 脱离出来后的发展历程。文章介绍了 FLUX 3 如何同时利用图像、视频和音频三种信号进行训练，以构建视觉智能；文中以接球为例说明，人们无法写下球的运动轨迹，却能根据运动和声音推断情况。两位创始人还谈到他们在扩散模型与自回归模型之间的技术选择、Kontext 实验如何通过关系学习教会模型画出戴帽子的狗，以及照片修复等意想不到的应用场景。此外，他们还回顾了从 Stability AI 转型至 BFL 的过程、视频升频中实现时间一致性的工程挑战，以及构建世界动作模型和机器人技术的长期愿景。

mainPoints.point: FLUX 3 同时利用图像、视频和音频三种信号进行训练，以构建视觉智能
mainPoints.explanation: 模型结合静态图像、动态影像和音轨进行学习，因此能够理解运动与时序，超越单帧分析所能达到的水平。例如，即使摄像机没有拍到球与物体接触的瞬间，音频也能表明球何时撞上了物体。

mainPoints.point: 视频升频离不开时间一致性，因此需要采用共享主干架构
mainPoints.explanation: 传统升频工具若独立锐化每一帧，连贯播放时可能会产生闪烁。BFL 的视频升频工具使用与 FLUX 3 相同的主干网络来保持帧间一致性，从而确保视频能以更高分辨率流畅播放。

mainPoints.point: Kontext 实验证明，关系学习能够教会模型理解构图
mainPoints.explanation: 通过使用标注了关系的照片进行训练，模型学会了把标志放在衬衫上，也学会了画出戴帽子的狗。这表明结构化数据无需显式编程，也能教会模型进行空间与上下文推理。

mainPoints.point: 用户反馈带来了照片修复等意想不到的应用场景
mainPoints.explanation: 用户将受损的家庭照片交给 FLUX 修复，这表明对人们而言，在编辑过程中以及不同帧之间保留人物身份至关重要，也为未来模型开发的优先方向提供了参考。

mainPoints.point: 团队根据训练成本与推理速度之间的权衡，选择了扩散模型而非自回归模型
mainPoints.explanation: 自回归模型可以在训练示例中一次使用所有 token，而扩散模型则能将漫长的采样过程蒸馏为仅需几步。因此，选择取决于成本主要花在训练上，还是花在等待结果上。

keyQuotes: 如果有人朝你扔来一个球，在球到达你之前，你的手就已经开始移动了。即使你无法写下球的运动轨迹，也能做到这一点。
静态图像能告诉你球在哪里，视频能展示它是怎么到那里的。撞击声则能告诉你球何时撞上了什么东西，即使摄像机没有拍到接触的瞬间。
如果独立锐化片段中的每一帧，每一帧都可能看起来很出色。但播放起来时，新增的细节可能会闪烁，因为升频工具每次处理时做出的判断都略有不同。
他猜想，一个能画出戴帽子狗的图像模型，应该已经知道帽子通常会戴在哪里。
